findings.title: Residency ledger maintains a `win` rolling-sum no read ever consumes — dual bookkeeping, one source of truth
findings.evidence: record pass: `r.win[key] -= u64(r.ticks[slot])` ... `r.ticks[slot] += 1; r.win[key] += 1`; read (port_residency_ticks) recomputes from the slot ring and never reads win values: `sum: u64 = 0; base := int(key) * RESIDENCY_WINDOW_TICKS; for s in 0..<RESIDENCY_WINDOW_TICKS { if r.slot_tick[base + s] > lo && r.slot_tick[base + s] <= tick { sum += u64(r.ticks[base + s]) } } return sum`. Grep over core/app/harness (incl. tests): `win`'s values are only written, resized, cloned (app/render/spawn_fx.odin:227), and length-checked (`if int(key) >= len(r.win)`), never read.
findings.detail: Maintained-never-read state: extra work per record tick, a second (stale-inclusive) sum that can never substitute for the staleness-filtered read, and a misleading comment in port_residency_ticks that reasons about `win`. Same debt class the review swarm removed (`bundle_class_queue`).
findings.recommended_fix: Delete the `win` field, its layout zero pass, and the two maintenance lines in residency_record_tick; keep the slot ring as the single source (bundle_tx_window's shape).

findings.title: packet_demand_units u32 wrap guard bounds bandwidth_demand only — packet_bandwidth (the other operand) is validated >0 with no upper bound
findings.evidence: core/flow.odin:601: `return u32(demand) * u32(cat.balance.packet_bandwidth)`. core/catalog.odin:630-635: `// ... bound it at load so the product can never wrap (an authoring-time // silent wrap would corrupt the AD-3(c) serialization term; 4096 x // 800 = 3.3M << 2^32, and no real frame is 4096 jumbo-frames wide). if bw > 4096 { return {"packet_types.json", pt.id, "bandwidth_demand must be 1..4096 (the u32 demand-total bound)"} }`. core/catalog.odin:863-866: `b.packet_bandwidth = jint(obj, "packet_bandwidth", 30) if b.packet_bandwidth <= 0 { return {"balance.json", "packet_bandwidth", "must be > 0 ..."} }`
findings.detail: A catalog passing all validation (demand 4096, packet_bandwidth 1048576 — only `<= 0` is rejected) wraps the u32 product; at exactly 2^32 it wraps to 0, serve_bundle_lane's need=0 skips the packet forever — never served, never dropped.
findings.recommended_fix: Complete the guard at load: reject packet_bandwidth > 2^32/4096 (1048576), or widen the multiply to u64 in packet_demand_units (and transit_ticks' demand_units+capacity-1 addition).

findings.title: Demand-wrap guard bounds only one multiplicand: packet_bandwidth has no upper bound at catalog load
findings.detail: The new bound closes the u32 wrap for the demand factor only. packet_bandwidth >= 2^32/4096 = 1,048,576 still silently wraps the product, corrupting the serialization term the comment claims can never wrap.
findings.recommended_fix: Validate the product jointly at load: bound packet_bandwidth (e.g. <= 1,048,575) or fail-fast when max_class_demand x packet_bandwidth would exceed u32 max.
